subject: science
chapterName: The Invisible Living World: Beyond Our Naked Eye
topicName: 2. Levels of Organisation in Living Organisms
explanation: Living organisms are highly organized. A complex organism like a human being is not made up of cells randomly arranged together. Instead, cells are organized into different levels, each performing specific functions. The levels of organization are: Cell to Tissue to Organ to Organ System to Organism. Each level is built from the previous one. A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of life, and every living organism begins as a single cell. A fertilized human egg starts as one cell and divides into millions of cells to form a complete baby; the ostrich egg is one of the largest known single cells. A tissue is a group of similar cells working together, such as muscle tissue (movement), nervous tissue (carries messages), and blood tissue (transports oxygen and nutrients); in plants, xylem transports water and phloem transports food. Different tissues combine to form an organ, such as the heart (pumps blood), lungs (breathing), stomach (digestion), leaf (makes food), and root (absorbs water). Several organs work together to form an organ system, such as the digestive system, respiratory system, and circulatory system. When all organ systems work together, they form a complete organism such as a human, dog, or mango tree. Organization makes life efficient because each part performs a specific task and the body functions smoothly.
examples: The correct sequence of organization is Cell to Tissue to Organ to Organ System to Organism.
A group of similar cells forms a tissue, such as muscle tissue for movement.
The heart is an organ that pumps blood throughout the body.
The respiratory system (nose, trachea, lungs) helps us breathe.

brainstorming.question: How can a single cell become a complete human body?
brainstorming.answer: A single fertilized egg continuously divides into millions of cells. These cells specialize and form tissues, organs, and organ systems.

brainstorming.question: Why can't individual cells perform all functions in humans?
brainstorming.answer: Humans are very complex organisms. Different cells specialize in different tasks, making body functions more efficient.

brainstorming.question: What would happen if organs worked independently?
brainstorming.answer: The body would not function properly because organs depend on each other and must work together in organ systems.

brainstorming.question: Why is the ostrich egg considered special?
brainstorming.answer: The ostrich egg is one of the largest single cells found in nature.

misconceptions.correct: Cells first form tissues, then organs, then organ systems, and finally an organism.

misconceptions.wrong: All tissues perform the same work.
One organ can perform every function.
misconceptions.correct: Different organs specialize in different tasks.

activities.title: Observe Different Levels in Your Body
activities.instructions: Identify a cell (conceptually), a tissue (muscle tissue), an organ (heart), and an organ system (circulatory system). Draw a flow chart showing the relationship. Observation: Students understand how small units combine to form larger structures. Conclusion: Living organisms are organized into different levels, making body functions efficient and coordinated.

options: Organ to Cell to Tissue to Organism
Cell to Tissue to Organ to Organ System to Organism
Tissue to Cell to Organ to Organism
Organism to Organ System to Organ
quiz.explanation: The correct order is Cell to Tissue to Organ to Organ System to Organism.

quiz.question: A group of similar cells forms:
quiz.explanation: A group of similar cells working together forms a tissue.

quiz.question: Which of the following is an organ?
quiz.explanation: The heart is an organ made of different tissues working together.

quiz.question: Which organ system helps in breathing?
quiz.explanation: The respiratory system helps in breathing.
